REGULATION No 019/R/ICT/RURA/2024 GOVERNING MOBILE NUMBER
PORTABILITY IN RWANDA
The Regulatory Board;
Pursuant to Law no 09/2013 of 01/03/2013 establishing Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority
(RURA) and determining its Mission, Powers, Organisation and Functioning, especially in
Article 2 and 20;
Pursuant to Law no 24/2016 of 18/06/2016 governing Information and Communication
Technologies, especially in Article 79;
Pursuant to Law no 058/2021 of 13/10/2021 relating to the protection of personal data and
privacy, especially in articles 17 and 50;
Noting that the adoption of mobile number portability regulation is necessary for enabling
consumers to easily choose the service provider that best meets their needs, while retaining
their mobile phone numbers;
Based on the recommendations made during the consultative meeting held on 25/09/2024
between RURA and different stakeholders in telecommunications sector;
Upon due consideration and deliberation in its session of 04/10 /2024;
HEREBY ISSUES THE FOLLOWING REGULATION:
CHAPTER ONE: GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article One: Purpose of this Regulation
(1) The purpose of this Regulation is to:
(a) put in place mechanisms and processes to allow all mobile phone subscribers in the Republic
of Rwanda to port their phone numbers when moving from one mobile Operator to another;
(b) determine the terms and conditions which shall be fulfilled by the operators of publicly
available electronic communications services to offer number portability;
(c) establish measures to make the switching process easy, secure and fast for the benefit of the
Switching Subscriber while retaining their numbers;
2

(d) guarantee the implementation of the mobile number portability service by all operators
providing mobile communications services and creating conditions for increasing and
protecting competition in the Republic of Rwanda telecommunication market.
Article 2: Scope of this Regulation
This Regulation applies to all licensed providers of electronic communications network or
electronic communications services, with assigned block numbers for their Networks.
Article 3: Interpretation
The following expressions, phrases and acronyms used in this Regulation shall have the
meaning provided below:
(a) ‘’Ageing Period’’ means the timeframe for a telephone number which has become inactive
with the Recipient Operator and cannot be assigned or used by Subscribers, to avoid misdialing;
(b) ‘’All Call Query (ACQ)’’ means direct traffic routing where the originating network, prior to
establishing any call or SMS, determines the network to which the called number is currently
located. All Call Query direct routing shall be used for all traffic originated and terminated in
Rwanda;
(c) ‘’Central Reference Data Base (CRDB)’’ is a database component within the Number
Portability Clearinghouse which stores the current network hosting status of every non-ported
and ported mobile number in Rwanda and contains the necessary information for the call
routing. All this information is updated in real time each time a mobile number is ported in
Rwanda;
(d) ‘’CLI validation’’ means the process where the number stated in the porting request has to
match the Subscriber’s CLI (Calling Line Identification). For mobile number ports, the
Subscriber will send a validation SMS to a specially allocated short code number owned by the
NPC service provider. This validation SMS will be free of charge to the Subscriber and will be
processed by the Donor Operator even if the Subscriber has a zero balance on their account.
The Subscriber’s CLI validation message will be verified by the NPC in accordance with the
porting process specified by the Regulatory Authority;
(e) ‘’Cooling Off’’ means the Subscriber’s right to cancel a new contract to which it has ported its
number and have the number returned to its previous Operator (the Donor Operator);
(f) ‘’Donor Operator’’ the Operator to whom the mobile number belongs at the time the
Subscriber makes a request for porting;
(g) ‘’Eligible Debt’’ refers to categories of debt which are defined in the Business Rules;
(h) ‘’ETSI’’ means European Telecommunications Standard Institute;
3

(i) ‘’Extra Conveyance Costs’’ are the specific extra costs incurred by an operator to convey
traffic to ported numbers compared to conveying traffic to non-ported numbers, including but
not limited to transit (signaling) and the database look up costs;
(j) ‘’LMDB’’ means ‘’Local Mirror Data Base’’, as the database maintained by each Operator,
connected to the CRDB which is updated in real-time by the NPC as each mobile number is
ported and contains the necessary information for the ACQ direct call routing to non-ported
and ported numbers;
(k) “MNP” means Mobile Number Portability, as the possibility of a mobile network subscriber to
retain a number of which the subscriber is granted to use on the basis of a subscription contract
if the subscriber changes the provider of electronic communications services or the
geographical location of use of the communications service;
(l) ‘’NBAO’’ means ‘’Number Block Allocated Operator’’, as the operator to which the
Regulatory Authority originally allocated the numbering block which contains the ported
number(s);
(m) ‘’NPC’’ means ‘’Number Portability Clearinghouse’’, as the entity engaged by the Operators
and licensed by the Regulatory Authority to operate the mobile number portability
administration service and centralised database which manage the delivery of number
portability services in Rwanda;
(n) ‘’Number Porting’’ means the execution of the number portability on request of the
subscriber;
(o) ‘’Numbering Plan’’ means the regulated framework overseen by the Regulatory Authority
which defines and manages the use of telephone numbering resources within Rwanda;
(p) ‘’Onward Routing’’ means the indirect traffic routing in which traffic is forwarded to the
Number Block Allocated Operator, which then determines if the called number is ported and
then routes and conveys the traffic to the Receiving Operator. Onward Routing is only permitted
for the conveyance of international incoming traffic;
(q) ‘’Onward Porting Period’’ the minimum timeframe managed by the NPC for which the
Subscriber is obliged to stay with the operator to whom they ported, before being permitted to
submit a new porting request to another operator;
(r) ‘’Operator’’ means a licensed entity which provides mobile services in the Republic of
Rwanda;
(s) ‘’Photo Identification’’ means the Regulatory Authority approved forms of identity document
that include a photograph of the holder, particularly his or her face, as specified in the
Regulation Governing SIM Card Registration in Rwanda dated 09/08/2024 as may be amended
from time to time;
4

(t) ‘’Porting Request Form’’ means a legal instrument signed by or on behalf of the Subscriber,
in which the Subscriber requests porting, and appoints the Recipient Operator as their agent to
port their number(s) from the Donor Operator and close their account with the Donor Operator.
The Porting Request Form may be digital or hardcopy paper;
(u) ‘’Post-paid Subscriber’’ means a Subscriber with post-paid services;
(v) ‘’Pre-paid Subscriber’’ means a Subscriber with pre-paid services;
(w) ‘’Recipient Operator’’ means the operator who will be providing the electronic
communications service to the subscriber after porting;
(x) ‘’Regulatory Authority ‘’– means the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority (RURA) as
established by Law no 09/2013 of 01/03/2013 establishing the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory
Authority (RURA) and determining its Mission, Powers, Organisation and Functioning, as may
be amended from time to time;
(y) Set-up Cost means the one-off extra cost incurred by the Donor Operator which is directly
attributable on a per number or line basis to port one or more numbers in addition to the cost to
transfer Subscribers to another operator without number portability or to terminate the
electronic communications service;
(z) ‘’SMS’’ means ‘’Short Message Service’’, as text messaging service component of phone,
Web, or mobile communication systems, which uses standardized communications protocols
to allow mobile phone devices to exchange short text messages;
(aa) ‘’Subscriber’’ means any natural person or legal entity who or which is party to a contract or
who accept the applicable Terms and Conditions with the provider of publicly available
electronic communications services for the supply of such services;
(bb) ‘’Switching Subscriber’’ means the subscriber, who submits the request to port their
mobile number(s);
(cc) ‘’Win-back’’ means contact initiated by the Donor Operator towards a Subscriber who has
either requested number portability, or who has already ported their number, where that contact
has the intention or effect of encouraging that Subscriber to remain with or return to the Donor
Operator;
(dd) ‘’Yearly cost of the Number Portability Administration Service’’ means the total
cost to enable, manage and maintain the Number Portability Clearinghouse Service in Rwanda.
CHAPTER II: GENERAL PRINCIPLES
Article 4: Impact on the numbering Plan
(1) Mobile numbers can only be ported and the porting of fixed (landline) to fixed (landline) or
mobile to fixed (landline) will not be permitted.
5

(2) The Recipient Operator uses the ported number to offer its services. The Recipient Operator is
responsible for the usage of the ported number.
(3) A ported number can only be used in accordance with the rules and principles as defined in the
National Numbering Plan for Electronic Communications Networks in the Republic of
Rwanda, approved by the Regulatory Authority.
(4) The operator who is responsible for the payment of numbering fees for ported numbers as
imposed by the National Numbering Plan shall be determined in the Business Rules.
(5) If the difference between ported in and ported out numbers from and to Recipient Operators is
expected to be significant, the working group can include in the industry wide business rules a
section stating that the Number Block Allocated Operator or Donor Operator has a right to
reclaim in a proportional way the fees as imposed by the Numbering Plan from a Recipient
Operator.
(6) If the contract between the Recipient Operator and the Subscriber terminates or the ported
number becomes inactive, as defined in the SIM Card registration regulation in force, and the
number is not subject to a subsequent porting, then in order to avoid erroneous calls the number
returns after an Ageing Period between a minimum of three (3) months and a maximum six
(6) months to the NBAO as stipulated under clause 8.13. During the Ageing Period, the
Recipient Operator will inform the caller that the Subscriber called number cannot be reached.
(7) Operators may at their discretion offer a facility to calling Subscribers before a call is
established to identify a called number as off-net.
Article 5: Exception Cases
Number portability cannot be requested and processed in the following scenarios:
(a) no first call has been made by a Pre-paid mobile Subscriber;
(b) during the Ageing Period;
(c) Subscriber has unsettled Eligible Debt;
(d) Any other reason determined in the Business Rules.
CHAPTER III: TECHNICAL AND OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS
Article 6: General requirements
(1) The porting of mobile numbers within Rwanda will be completed within a maximum of one (1)
porting day from the point the NPC validated porting request is passed to the Donor operator for
approval.
6

(2) Each Operator is obliged to implement an LMDB, which will contain the routing information for
all non-ported and ported numbers in the Republic of Rwanda. The LMDB should be synchronized
with the CRDB in real-time each time a mobile number is ported as notified by the NPC, as defined
by clause 10.3.
(3) Each Operator is obliged to check the synchronization of their LMDB against the CRDB every
week, using synchronization files provided by the NPC.
(4) Each Operators is free to decide their own network architecture, network functions and other
specifications except for those on the common interfaces as determined in paragraph (3) of this
article. The procedures defined by chapter IV of this Regulation will be provided by the Regulatory
Authority and finalised in collaboration with the Operators within the industry wide business rules;
the final version will be approved by the Regulatory Authority management.
(5) The NPC service provider will provide the specifications on the common interfaces for the
interworking with Operator systems, provide a description of the network architecture and the
relevant service level performance metrics. This document/these documents shall be approved by
the Regulatory Authority management. The signaling and network architecture will be based on
ETSI specifications. The specifications as defined in paragraph (3) of this article will be published
on the Regulatory Authority website.
Article 7: The Routing Process
(1) The method of routing traffic to all non-ported and ported numbers originated and terminated in the
Republic of Rwanda for operators with mobile services will be the All Call Query (ACQ) routing
method.
(2) Calls to ported numbers will be routed through routing numbers (RN) defined in the Republic of
Rwanda Numbering Plan allocated and approved by the Regulatory Authority.
(3) An Operator of an electronic communications network which receives international originated
incoming calls or SMS text or multimedia messages to a ported number shall be responsible for the
correct Onward Routing of such traffic directly to the current Recipient Operator.
Article 8: Number Portability Clearinghouse (NPC) and Central Reference Data Base
(CRDB)
(1) All Operators using E.164 mobile numbers to offer public electronic communications services are
obliged to implement and use their own LMDB synchronized with the CRDB, by processing routing
update broadcast messages from the NPC (in real-time as each number is ported) and on a weekly
basis with the synchronization files provided by the NPC. Each Operator’s LMDB supports the
operational processes and contains the routing information necessary to directly route traffic to non-
ported and ported numbers using the ACQ direct routing approach.
(2) Emergency services may be provided with free of charge (online) access to the CRDB via the NPC
subject to the Regulatory Authority approval. All CRDB routing and NPC porting information will
7

be stored for the duration of the license assigned by the Regulatory Authority to the selected NPC
provider.
(3) The Regulatory Authority and selected Operators will select an operational provider to offer the
NPC services to all the relevant stakeholders. The selection process will be led by the Regulatory
Authority and managed in an open, transparent and professional manner to attract world-class NPC
service providers. The final selection of the operational provider of NPC services will be approved
by the Regulatory Authority.
(4) The NPC service will be located in the Republic of Rwanda with the main location being a suitable
datacenter in Kigali. A second back-up data centre will also be established at a separate location for
resilience purposes. The NPC service will be operated in compliance with the Rwanda data
protection laws and regulations.
(5) The set-up and operation of the NPC service will be jointly funded by the Regulatory Authority and
the Operators. The Regulatory Authority funding contribution of the NPC will be the Set-up and
shall be funded through the Universal Access Fund, while the Operators’ direct financial
contribution will be towards the operations of the NPC.
(6) The Regulatory Authority may at its discretion mandate the local management of the NPC service
to a licensed Rwandan third-party company/ organization. The remaining non-RURA funded NPC
operational costs will be managed using a cost sharing/ allocation framework and multi-party
contract approved by the Regulatory Authority. The Regulatory Authority will not be party to the
cost sharing/ allocation framework and multi-party contract.
(7) The selected NPC service provider will be licensed by the Regulatory Authority to provide the NPC
service in Rwanda.
(8) The operation of the NPC service must be compliant with the relevant Data Protection legislation
and regulations prevailing or introduced during the term of the multi-party NPC service contract.
CHAPTER IV: ADMINISTRATIVE PORTING PROCESS
Article 9: Basic Principles
(1) For porting a number, the following consecutive steps have to be followed in addition to the
requirements for registering a SIM card as specified in the Regulation governing SIM card
registration in Rwanda in force:
(a) The request of the Subscriber to the Recipient Operator;
(b) Verification of the Switching Subscriber’s Photo Identification. The Recipient Operator
will take a copy of the presented Photo Identification and retain it as required by the
Regulation;
8

(c) The Recipient Operator will verify that the Switching Subscriber is in possession of the
number(s) to be ported. In the case of porting requests involving multiple numbers, the
Recipient Operator should verify that the Switching Subscriber or in the case of non-
personal porting requests, the authorized/ delegated authority can demonstrate possession
of the number identified for the CLI validation for the overall porting request which is also
included in the porting transaction;
(d) For personal porting requests where the current mobile service is Post-paid with the Donor
Operator, the Recipient Operator will request the Switching Subscriber to provide a recent
bill from the Donor Operator and will verify the Subscriber name on the Donor Operator
bill matches the Switching Subscriber’s presented Photo Identification. In the case that the
presented Photo Identification does not match the name on the Donor Operator’s bill, the
Recipient Operator shall inform the Switching Subscriber that Number Portability cannot
be progressed;
(e) For non-personal porting requests, (porting requests involving numbers belonging to
companies or organisations), where the current mobile service is Post-paid with the Donor
Operator, the Recipient Operator will request the Switching Subscriber to provide a signed
letter of authority confirming them as either:
i) the designated account signatory with the Donor Operator, or
ii) delegated authority authorized by the designated account signatory with the Donor
Operator – Annex II. The Recipient Operator will verify if it matches with the
presented authorization letter and will take a copy of the Switching Subscriber’s
presented Photo Identification. In the case that the presented Photo Identification
does not match the authorisation letter, the Recipient Operator shall inform the
Switching Subscriber that Number Portability cannot be progressed. The Recipient
Operator may, at its discretion, send by email a copy of the signed authorisation
letter (See Annex II) to the Donor Operator to confirm the validity of the non-
personal porting request;
(f) The completion of an approved porting form (see Annex I). The completion and signature
by the Switching Subscriber of the approved porting form shall serve as limited power of
attorney authorizing Recipient Operator to close the Subscriber’s account with the Donor
Operator and to switch the Subscriber’s number to the Recipient Operator. The Recipient
Operator shall ensure the Switching Subscriber understands and acknowledges their
obligations to request Number Portability and the implications of using the Number
Portability service as defined in the approved Porting Form;
(g) Subscriber’s CLI validation by SMS;
(h) The request of the Recipient Operator submitted to the NPC to initiate the number porting
with the Donor Operator. The minimum information to be included in this request is: the
Donor Operator, whether the numbers to be ported are Pre-paid or Post-paid and E212
number(s) to be ported;
9

(i) The agreement of the Donor Operator to port the number which is confirmed during the
porting process and not beforehand;
(j) The installation and/or activation of the mobile number on the Recipient Operator’s
network followed by the actual porting of the number as signified by the transmission of
the routing broadcast message sent to the connected Operator LMDBs by the NPC;
(k) The update of the routing information in all the relevant Number Portability Databases
(CRDB and Operators’ LMDBs);
(l) The deactivation of the number by the Donor Operator.
(2) The Subscriber will be notified of the status and progress of their Porting request by the NPC at
defined stages in the porting process by SMS.
(3) The Subscriber who requests to port his/her number signs the written or electronic document,
which can be found in Annex 1 (named “Porting Form”) where the Subscriber:
(a) Identifies himself/ herself without any ambiguity with a valid identification document;
(b) Gives a mandate to the Recipient Operator to close the account with the Donor Operator
and to port their number to the Recipient Operator’s network;
(c) Is informed that his/her request to port will be refused by the Donor Operator in case their
number or account is subject to unsettled Eligible Debt or for any other ground for refusal
provided for in this Regulation and may be subject to the dunning process;
(d) Is informed that in case of a prepaid mobile subscription, they will lose any remaining
airtime credit at the time of porting from the Donor Operator;
(e) Is informed that they may lose undelivered SMS/ MMS messages at the time of porting;
(f) Is informed that they may not receive the same services that are provided by the Donor
Operator;
(g) Is informed that voicemail services and associated messages may be lost;
(h) Is informed that they have to respect the terms and conditions of the contract, and that they
could be subject to a penalty.
(4) The Regulatory Authority has the right to check and make changes to the Porting Form in order to
ensure the compliance with this Regulation.
(5) The Regulatory Authority and/ or the Donor Operator has the right to ask for sight of the completed
and signed Porting Form for any porting request from the Recipient Operator within a notice of two
(2) working days in order to check complaints of Subscriber (e.g. slamming) or to verify the
compliance with this Regulation.
10

(6) The completed Porting Form and associated Photo Identification and authorization letter (non-
personal ports only) must be stored by the Recipient Operator for a period of ten (10) years after
the date of signature.
(7) The Subscriber can only port a previously ported number after the Onward Porting Period expires.
The Onward Porting Period is ninety (90) calendar days from the date of the completion of the last
porting transaction for the given number. The Onward Porting Period restrictions will be managed
by the NPC, which will validate eligibility once the Recipient Operator’s porting request has been
validated with the corresponding CLI validation.
(8) The Donor Operator is prohibited from initiating contact with a Subscriber who has either requested
number portability, or who has already ported their number, where that contact has the intention or
effect of encouraging that Subscriber to remain with or return to the Donor Operator. This excludes
contact made for the recovery of outstanding debts or balances from that Subscriber. Win-back is
prohibited for ninety (90) calendar days after the port is completed (from the point the NPC sends
the broadcast message) plus the initial period from the point when the NPC sends the porting
approval request to the Donor Operator until the port is completed.
(9) If the Recipient Operator starts the porting process without authorisation of the Subscriber, then in
the case the number is already ported, the number will be returned back to the Donor Operator as
soon as possible.
(10) The overall porting time window will be from the moment the NPC sends the validated porting
approval request to the Donor Operator for approval until the moment the Donor Operator confirms
the ported number has been deactivated after the NPC has sent the routing update broadcast message
to the connected LMDBs, and it should be as short as possible.
(11) All Operators are required to establish and operate interworking functions with the NPC which
enable Number Portability transactions to be processed automatically through the defined Number
Portability process to conclusion after the porting approval request is sent by the Recipient Operator
to the NPC.
(12) Once a ported number has become inactive with the Recipient Operator and has completed the
Ageing Process, the Recipient Operator is not permitted to allocate the ported number to another
Subscriber and is obliged to return the ported number to the NBAO via the NPC using the process
described in the industry wide business rules.
(13) Within a maximum of one (1) month of a non-ported or ported number becoming inactive or
following contract termination with the current or Recipient Operator, at the request of the validated
Subscriber, the current or Recipient Operator will reactivate the number to enable the Subscriber to
port the number to another Operator.
(14) Subscribers will be permitted to invoke Cooling Off provisions to port back to the previous
Donor Operator, the Cooling-off period for mobile number portability in the Republic of Rwanda
is seven (7) calendar days from the date of their last porting transaction. By invoking Cooling Off
provisions, the Subscriber is obliged to pay for call charges, to pay early termination charges, or to
return any equipment that is part of a service package to the Recipient Operator.
11

Article 10: Validation Phase
(1) After the signature by the Subscriber of the completed Porting Form, there follows the submission
by the Recipient Operator’s porting approval request and the submission by the Subscriber of the
CLI validation, both sent to the NPC.
(2) Once the NPC successfully matches the Recipient Operator’s porting approval request with the
corresponding Subscriber’s CLI validation SMS, the NPC will verify that the validated porting
request is correct and eligible for Number Portability before sending to the Donor Operator for
approval.
(3) The Donor Operator can only reject the request to port in the following cases:
(a) The Subscriber’s number to be ported is subject to unsettled Eligible Debts and may be
subject to the dunning process in the Donor Operator’s network;
(b) The number to be ported is not active with the Donor Operator;
(c) The number to be ported has been reported as stolen or lost.
(4) The following maximum time window for the validation of a mobile number porting request by
the Donor Operator (validation time) has to be respected: maximum four (4) hours during
working days on receipt by the Donor Operator of the porting request from the NPC.
(5) A working day starts from Monday to Friday (9.00 till 17.00 hours), excluding public holidays
and weekends. The porting time window starts when the NPC submits the validated porting
approval request to the Donor Operator.
(6) In conformance with this Regulation, the details of the validation process will be described in the
Business rules specifications.
(7) The volume of numbers to be ported may be limited by the Regulatory Authority at any time.
Article 11: Activation of the number porting
(1) Activated is the status where a Subscriber who ports his/her number can make and receive calls
from all networks.
(2) In case of mobile porting requests, the maximum activation time is four (4) hours once the Donor
Operator has confirmed approval of the validated porting approval request, requiring the
Recipient Operator to activate the service on its network.
(3) Operators are required to automatically update connected LMDBs within two (2) minutes of
received routing broadcast messages from the NPC for each successfully completed porting
transaction.
12

(4) In conformance of this Regulation, the details of the activation process will be described in the
Business rules specifications.
Article 12: Subscriber compensation
(1) Subscribers have a right to compensation in case of a delay in number porting. For Pre-paid and
Post-paid mobile subscriptions, the compensation amount per number per day of delay will be
included in the Business rules.
(2) The delay starts when deadlines for timeframes stated in 9.4, 10.2 and 10.3 expire.
(3) The total compensation is per day compensation multiplied by the number of working days that
the porting is delayed.
(4) The Recipient Operator is responsible for the administrative handling of the complaint and
payment of the compensation.
(5) The Recipient Operator can reclaim the penalty from the Operator which is the cause of the delay.
(6) In case of abuse, the Regulatory Authority will determine the compensation for the Subscriber to
be paid by the Operator which is the cause of the abuse to the complaining Subscriber.
CHAPTER V: FINANCIAL ASPECTS
Article 13: Number portability charges for the Subscriber’s number
(1) Neither the Recipient Operator nor the Donor Operator will be allowed to charge the Subscriber
for the number porting. If they wish, the Recipient Operator will be allowed to charge the
Subscriber for the new SIM card a fee not exceeding the current SIM swap price.
(2) Once the Number Portability process is concluded and the number is ported, the Subscriber’s
contract with the Donor Operator will be terminated with immediate effect.
Article 14: Wholesale tariffs between Operators and the financing of Number Portability
Clearinghouse Services
(1) Each Operator bears their own system set up cost for introducing Number Portability in its
network and adaptation of its operational systems.
(2) The charge levied by the Donor Operator on the Recipient Operator for processing a porting out
request per mobile number is based on an efficient Number Portability process and may only be
set and charged by the Donor Operator to the Recipient Operator after approval by the Regulatory
Authority.
(3) The Recipient Operator may compensate the NBAO or any other operator for the relevant extra
conveyance cost of routing international incoming traffic to a ported number, subject to the prior
written approval of the Regulatory Authority.
13

(4) From the public launch of the Number Portability service, the yearly incremental operational cost
of the NPC services beyond the initial funding by the Regulatory Authority from the Universal
Access Fund will be covered by operators using a cost allocation mechanism agreed by the NPC
operator, the Rwanda mobile operators and approved by the Regulatory Authority.
(5) Before the public launch of the Number Portability service, the NPC operator and the Rwanda
mobile operators will submit a cost allocation mechanism for the operation of the NPC. If the
NPC operator and the Rwanda mobile operators are unable to agree on an NPC cost allocation
mechanism, the Regulatory Authority will determine the mechanism for the allocation of NPC
service costs between the operators.
Article 15: Administrative Sanctions
In case of breach of the provisions of this Regulation, the Regulatory authority shall apply
sanctions provided for under the Law governing Information Communication Technologies
and/or the Law establishing the Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority where applicable.
CHAPTER VI: FINAL PROVISIONS
Article 16: Transitional period for Introduction of Number Portability
(1) The Number Portability for mobile telephony subscribers will be introduced after the Regulatory
Authority has approved the technical documents in conformance with 5.3.1 and 5.3.2 of this
Regulation.
(2) All Operators have the right to participate and collaborate in an industry wide working group and
programme led by the Regulatory Authority to progress the development, implementation, launch
and operationalisation of the Number Portability service in the Republic of Rwanda.
(3) All Operators are mandated to comply with the key industry wide Number Portability programme
